### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **6** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **30** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/object.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/object.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**32** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 83bd36decf7daef4e07f430326cb50c33762c278`.

⛔ **14** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/object.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/object.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `resolveObjectMasker (5 routes)`
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **182** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 83bd36decf7daef4e07f430326cb50c33762c278` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fcff2211e4165ab08b8ad320b5c7965632b930a3` — the merge of head `b8880188109b3c070e25f978aa539cac5e509a83` into base `83bd36decf7daef4e07f430326cb50c33762c278`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin fcff2211e4165ab08b8ad320b5c7965632b930a3 && git checkout fcff2211e4165ab08b8ad320b5c7965632b930a3
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 83bd36decf7daef4e07f430326cb50c33762c278 b8880188109b3c070e25f978aa539cac5e509a83 && git checkout -B drift-repro 83bd36decf7daef4e07f430326cb50c33762c278 && git merge --no-ff b8880188109b3c070e25f978aa539cac5e509a83

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 83bd36decf7daef4e07f430326cb50c33762c278
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 83bd36decf7daef4e07f430326cb50c33762c278` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ff77f21ea058b75ed070970f916496ce7103aa4b`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts, docs/adr/0106-metadata-plane-fls-object-schema-masking.md + packages/metadata-core/src/object-schema-fls.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/object-schema-fls-references.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-api-plugin.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts, packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts, packages/mcp/src/plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/sys-approval-request.object.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/sys-approval-action.object.ts, scripts/adr-anchors/packages__metadata-core__src__object-schema-fls.ts.json

Read for this record: card #32955 (its body and all five comments; decision 6840464379 binds), this PR's body, file list and net diff against `main`, and the check-runs on the head as they stood at 2026-11-13T04:55Z. Code outside the diff was read, never reviewed. The rest of the diff (tests, generated spec artifacts, `content/docs/**`, the engine-double pin) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

**Result: two must-fix findings. Two `Test Core` shards are red on this head because of the new key (① items 3 and 9). The design in ④ held under every attack tried and carries four nits. Security findings: none, and nothing is withheld from this record.**

### ① Derived judgments

Gate verdicts concluded on this head:

- `success`: `Lint & Repo Gates` with all eight `Lint ·` lanes, `TypeScript Type Check` with all four `Type Check ·` lanes, `Type Check UI`, `Build Core`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`, `Build Docs`, `Spec property liveness`, `Check Changeset` (both runs), `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` (the PR-speed run; its shards run in the queue), `Test UI` with all sixteen shards, and `Test Core` shards 1, 3, 4, 5 and 7.
- `failure`: `Test Core (2/8)` and `Test Core (6/8)`.
- Not concluded: `Test Core (8/8)`. `Lint UI` is skipped.

What the diff implies, each judged:

1. **Right.** `ObjectSchema` accepts one more optional string key, `schemaReadDelegate`. `authorable-surface/data.json` gains `data/Object:schemaReadDelegate`, the liveness ledger classifies it `live` against evidence that exists at the head, and the reference pages are regenerated. No export is added, so the spec's api-surface rightly does not move.
2. **Right, and load-bearing.** `ObjectExtensionSchema` does not gain the key. It is its own strict object, and `mergeObjectDefinitions` copies a closed set, so an extending package cannot put the key on an object it does not own.
3. **Wrong as shipped (M1, must-fix).** The schema accepts the key, and the object form neither offers it nor records why not. `Test Core (2/8)` fails on it, in `packages/spec/src/system/metadata-form-zod-reconciliation.test.ts`: `object.(root): accepted by the Zod but unauthorable in the form — offer it, or add a root ledger entry that records why it is not offered`, naming `schemaReadDelegate`. This is a contract choice, and the diff did not make it. Under ADR bullet 7 as this head carries it, the consistent answer is the ledger row: a declaration is a recorded exception, and it names a service only code can provide. Offering the key in the Studio form, as the precedent key `fileAccessDelegate` is offered, would hand every author the declaration that bullet reserves. If the maintainer softens the bullet, this choice reopens.
4. **Right.** `packages/metadata-core` publishes `ObjectSchemaReadDelegate`, `ObjectSchemaReadDelegateSource` and `objectSchemaReadDelegateSource` through its barrel, and `resolveObjectSchemaMaskPosture` takes an optional `schemaReadDelegates`. A caller that hands none gets the pre-PR answer.
5. **Right.** `RestServer` takes an optional last constructor argument, wired by `RestApiPlugin` and classified in the slot-lookup ledger.
6. **Right.** `createStdioDataBridge` and `callerObjectView` take an optional source. Neither is published by the package entry.
7. **Right.** `ApprovalService` gains the public method `authorizeSchemaRead`, and both objects' served definitions now carry the key (`OBJECT_REFERENCE_POSITIONS` keeps it: it names no field).
8. **Right.** For a caller the delegate admits, the two definitions move from absent to served on every schema-serving outlet. The posture has three call sites (REST, the dispatcher, stdio MCP) and all three hand it the source. No other caller's and no other object's answer moves.
9. **Wrong as shipped (M2, must-fix).** `GET /meta/types` serves the `object` type's schema with 50 top-level properties where it served 49. The move itself is right: the key belongs in the served schema. Its control pin did not move. `CARD_PROPERTY_COUNTS` in `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.meta-types-degenerate-derivation.test.ts` still says `object: 49`, and `Test Core (6/8)` fails on it: `control: object still serves 49 top-level properties`, `expected 50 to be 49`. Fix: move the pin to 50 with the count-move note that file keeps for every earlier key.

Both red suites, `packages/spec` and `packages/metadata-protocol`, are missing from the five the dev report ran, and both files are outside this PR's file list. `Test Core` is a required context, so this head cannot land. After both fixes, run the whole suite once (AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist step 1): `Test Core (8/8)` had not concluded when this was written, so this record cannot say these two are the only ones.

### ② Semver level

- The changeset takes `minor` on `packages/spec` and `packages/metadata-core`, and `patch` on rest, runtime, mcp and plugin-approvals. `Metadata-protocol: added` is right: one new authorable key, nothing removed, tightened or changed in meaning. `added` takes at least `minor` on the package that carries the key, and spec has it. `minor` on metadata-core is above its floor and allowed. The other four are non-protocol widenings and ship `patch`.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right: an accept set and several public surfaces widen and nothing narrows, so no BREAKING banner and no ADR-0087 disposition is owed.
- Both lines are line-initial and identical in the PR body and the changeset body, and `Check Changeset` is green. The seat claim 6840483971 said `Metadata-protocol: none`; the re-post 6842587846 corrected it to `added` before the PR opened, and the PR follows the newer claim.
- `Skills-docs: none` holds: no file under `skills/` teaches the precedent key either.
- Neither fix moves the level. A ledger row and a pin are test files and publish nothing, and offering the key in the form instead would stay inside the `minor` that spec already takes.

### ③ Boundary flags

Open questions in the os-dev report (6844043517):

- **Keep the ADR text in this PR, or split it:** escalated to the maintainer. The ADR text is Tier H either way.
- **Keep or soften the ADR's closing bullet:** escalated to the maintainer. This head carries the strict form, and ④ judged that form. M1's fix depends on the answer.
- **Drive the console now, or rely on round 2:** answered, rely on round 2, which decision item 1 makes mandatory on the frozen sha. Named plainly: the decision's third acceptance clause (the console request page renders its decision actions for that approver) is not evidenced at this head. The HTTP pin evidences the first two. One supporting read: the source under `ui/` names no approval object other than these two.

Dev flags:

- **A viewer admitted only by the record-reader tier still gets the absent answer.** Accepted for this PR: it fails closed and ADR bullet 6 records it. "Noted, not filed" is the wrong end state, though. If the record page's approvals panel needs the definitions for that read-only viewer, it has not rendered for them since #32428. Owed: a card. The tier is default off, so it does not block.
- **No index on `sys_approval_action.actor_id` or `acted_as`.** Accepted as outside this PR, but the stated reason undercounts. See nit N1. Owed: a card.
- **The dispatcher's service lookup folds a fault into "not registered".** Read in the tree and agreed. `domains/meta.ts` passes no scope id, so the chain stays on the request's own kernel, the same lookup `security` takes two lines above, and the host kernel answers only a request that carries no kernel of its own. It fails closed, and ADR bullet 5 records the fold.
- **`security_findings: none`.** This review found none either.
- **"CI check-runs are not read yet."** Read above: two red, M1 and M2.
- **An emptied projection stays a fault** (PR body). Agreed, and unchanged by this diff.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`: holds, apart from its form face (M1).** Against the decision: the exception is a declaration on the object, and no gate holds a name list. The key sits beside its precedent with the same shape. Its TSDoc agrees with the code clause by clause: asked only after the read check refused, `true` serves the definition under the caller's own projection, no row opens, a missing service or method leaves the object absent, a throw is the 5xx fault. Against its first consumer: both approval objects declare `'approvals'`, and `approvals-plugin.ts` registers the `ApprovalService` instance itself under that name, so the method is reachable through the same lookup the approvals door's own routes use.

**`docs/adr/0106-metadata-plane-fls-object-schema-masking.md`: holds.** Against the decision, item by item: #32428's rule is not reverted, the exception is declared by the owner, it is recorded against ruling record 6787890900 in the status line and its own section, rows stay behind `/api/v1/approvals/*`, field security applies, and every other object keeps `hidden`. Against its execution, bullet by bullet:

- Bullet 1: a census of the head finds exactly two declarations and one implementing service.
- Bullet 2: the posture module names no object, and the declaration is read through `getSchema` on every call. Agrees, with nit N3.
- Bullet 3: in `resolveObjectSchemaMaskPosture` the D8 switch returns first, then the D4 exemption, then the field posture, then `canReadObject`. The delegate is reached only when that did not answer `true`, is skipped on `undetermined`, and admits only on a literal `true`. Agrees.
- Bullet 4: an admitted caller's posture is their field posture itself, so every outlet serves them exactly as it serves a reader. Agrees.
- Bullet 5: no source, no declaration, no service and no method each answer `false`. The lookup and the verdict sit in one `try` whose catch raises `ObjectSchemaMaskEvaluationError`. Agrees, with nits N2 and N4.
- Bullet 6: `authorizeSchemaRead` refuses every name but its two. `servesAnyRequest` is `visibleRequestIds`, the rule `getRequest` applies, then one `sys_approval_request` read inside the caller's organization. The record-reader tier returns early without a named record. Agrees.
- Bullet 7: nothing mechanical enforces it, as the PR body says. It is the only thing that keeps "every other object keeps `hidden`" true for a future declaration.

**Implementing files: each agrees with the contract.**

- `object-schema-fls.ts`: as bullets 3 to 5. A deployment with an object read check and no field reader serves an admitted caller unprojected, exactly as it serves a reader there (D6 tier 1).
- `rest-server.ts` and `rest-api-plugin.ts`: the engine and the service are resolved for the same environment id `security` is, through `environmentScopedProvider`: an environment's request is answered by that environment's kernel or by nothing.
- `domains/meta.ts`: the dispatcher's masker, which the HTTP MCP object tools and the action run doors share. The action doors read the field half only (`objectSchemaFieldPosture`), so an admission moves no action verdict.
- `stdio-data-bridge.ts` and `mcp/plugin.ts`: both `callerObjectView` call sites carry the source. The data verbs read the unmasked view for their gates and serve none of it.
- `approval-service.ts`: as bullet 6. The verdict memo is keyed on the context object, and all three transports assemble a new context per request or per read, so a member who becomes a party is admitted on their next request.
- The two object files and the anchor invariant say what the code does.

**Attacks, each tried against the tree:**

1. *A member party to no request learns something new.* No. They get the same absent answer as before, on the item read and in every list. The verdict depends on the caller's own participation alone, which their own approvals inbox already tells them. Cross-organization: the approver index and the submitter probe carry the caller's organization; the already-acted probe does not, and the final request read applies it again. Every caller the predicate admits is one the door's own by-id read serves at least one request, or its override holder.
2. *Rows reach someone through some door.* No. The diff touches no data door, the posture has no caller that serves rows, and the HTTP pin holds the data door closed to the approver.
3. *Field security is skipped.* No. Admission returns the caller's own field posture, and an undetermined one never asks the delegate.
4. *Another object's `hidden` answer changes.* No. An object with no declaration returns before any service lookup, and the list asks the same masker per object, so a list and an item read cannot differ. The pin holds the approver's list equal to the stranger's plus the two.
5. *A tenant overlay or a third-party package declares the delegate on an object it does not own.* An extension cannot: item 2 above. A tenant overlay's body can carry the key, because the overlay is the base of the served fold. It unhides nothing: the only implementing service refuses every name but its two, a name with no implementing service stays absent, and only code can register a service. The pairing check is the delegate's own, which is what ADR bullet 6 says.
6. *The path when the delegate is absent or throws.* Absent or without the method: `hidden`, warned. Any answer but `true`: `hidden`. A throw: the 5xx fault, never an admission and never a false absence. On a list, that fault fails the list for the callers that object is hidden from, as a throwing `canReadObject` already does.

**Findings:**

- **M1, must-fix:** ① item 3, the form face of the new key. A FAIL.
- **M2, must-fix:** ① item 9, the `/meta/types` control pin. A FAIL.
- **N1, nit (follow-up card):** cost. Every object list read by a caller who cannot read the two objects, and every other outlet that asks the posture about them, now runs the approvals participant probe: up to five reads, one an unindexed scan of `sys_approval_action`, collecting up to three 10 000-row windows and sending them back as one `$in` to answer a yes or no. Before this PR only the approvals door's own reads paid it. No effect on correctness or the contract. A bounded existence probe and the index belong to one card.
- **N2, nit (accepted deviation):** the unusable-delegate notice is keyed on object and service name for the whole process and marks the key before it checks for a sink. A second environment kernel with the same misdeclaration is never told. All three wired outlets pass a sink, so the ADR's "said once" holds today.
- **N3, nit (prose):** ADR bullet 2 says the owner declares the exception. The definition a resolution reads is the served fold, which is a tenant overlay's body where one is registered. Nothing unhides through that (attack 5), and the precedent key is read the same way. The sentence would be exact if it named the layer.
- **N4, nit (prose):** `domains/meta.ts` says the two transports cannot disagree about the exception. They agree on every verdict. They differ on one fault: a registered service whose lookup fails is 5xx on REST's environment leg and absent on the dispatcher and stdio. ADR bullet 5 allows both.

The delta review owed covers the fixes of M1 and M2, and whatever else that lap moves.

Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4cwJbS8sZAfru2iyvQq`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b8880188109b3c070e25f978aa539cac5e509a83`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts, docs/adr/0106-metadata-plane-fls-object-schema-masking.md + packages/metadata-core/src/object-schema-fls.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/object-schema-fls-references.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-api-plugin.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts, packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts, packages/mcp/src/plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/sys-approval-request.object.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/sys-approval-action.object.ts, scripts/adr-anchors/packages__metadata-core__src__object-schema-fls.ts.json, packages/spec/src/system/metadata-form-zod-reconciliation.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.meta-types-degenerate-derivation.test.ts

Delta record. Round 1 is 6844571138 on `ff77f21e` (FAIL on M1 and M2). This head is one commit on top of that one, and this record judges that commit; everything round 1 judged outside it stands as written there.

Read for this record: round 1, the three-file diff between the two heads, the code those hunks cite, the card thread's run record for this head, and the check-runs on both heads as they stood at 2026-11-13T05:30Z. Nothing was built or run. The two test files join `Scope:` because round 1's must-fixes live in them.

**Result: M1 and M2 are fixed the way round 1 asked. N4 is fixed in a comment that reads true. No new finding. N1, N2 and N3 stay open as nits. Security findings: none, and nothing is withheld from this record.**

### ① Derived judgments

Check-runs on this head at 05:30Z: 16 `success` (among them `Check Changeset`, `Spec property liveness`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Type Check · source gates`), none failed, 20 not concluded. All eight `Test Core` shards started at 05:28Z and are in the 20. So M1 and M2 are judged below by reading the assertions against the tree, not by a concluded run, and landing reads the checks itself.

Round 1's open point is closed: `Test Core (8/8)` concluded `success` on `ff77f21e` at 05:03Z, so shards 2 and 6 were the only reds on that head.

What the delta implies, each judged:

1. **Right (M1).** The form reconciliation ledger gains one root `omit` row for `object.schemaReadDelegate`. `packages/spec/src/data/object.form.ts` is the same blob on both heads (`59ce62da`): the key is not offered. The row answers the assertion that was red (the root reconciliation drops a key a root `omit` row names) and passes the ledger's own checks as read: the key is authorable in the schema, no form row offers it, it is not an overlay field, and its reason opens with none of the three classes ruling record 5861442317 closed, so those key sets do not move.
2. **Right (M2).** `CARD_PROPERTY_COUNTS.object` is 50, the number shard 6 received on the round-1 head, with a `[#32955] 49 → 50` note in the form that file keeps for every earlier key. Nothing in the delta moves the served schema.
3. **Right.** The hunk in `packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts` changes comment lines only. No executable token moves.
4. **Nothing else moves.** `object.zod.ts` and the ADR are byte-identical to the round-1 head, as is every other file in round 1's `Scope:`. No published surface and no generated artifact is in the delta.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged from round 1, which judged these fixes in advance: two test files and a comment publish nothing. The changeset is not in the delta, and `Check Changeset` is green on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **The two maintainer questions stay escalated** (the ADR text in this PR or split; the closing bullet kept or softened). The M1 row is written against the strict bullet and repeats it. If the bullet is softened, the row and the form offer reopen together.
- **Still not evidenced at this head:** the third acceptance clause of decision 6840464379 (the console request page renders its decision actions for the approver). Round 2 owes it on the frozen sha.
- **Cards round 1 found owed stay owed:** the read-only viewer admitted only by the record-reader tier, and N1.
- **The run record for this head lists no test run.** It names fourteen commands, the repo gates, spec liveness and lint, each at exit 0. The whole-suite run round 1 asked for rests on CI here.

### ④ Design judgment

**`object.zod.ts`, the ADR and every implementing file but `domains/meta.ts`: unchanged. Round 1's judgment stands.**

**M1, the ledger row: holds.** Held against ADR bullet 7 as this head carries it: a later declaration is "a further exception to ruling record 6787890900, recorded here and reviewed against every rule above before it ships". The row's reason says that in the same terms and adds two facts that read true in the tree: the named service exists only where a plugin registers it (both approval objects declare `approvals` beside the service), and a declaration naming a service the deployment lacks leaves the object absent (bullet 5). Its header comment calls the key `live`, which is the liveness ledger's verdict, and cites the ADR section by its heading. The reason opens `live, reserved to code`, a reason of its own with its own authority; it does not borrow `code-declared platform configuration`, which admits only the keys its ruling named. The precedent key `fileAccessDelegate` stays offered in the same form. The two keys now differ on purpose, and the row says why.

**M2, the pin: holds.** One number and its note, as ① item 2.

**N4, the comment: holds, and closes N4.** Each claim was read in the tree. The dispatcher's service lookup returns nothing on any rejection, so the posture finds no usable delegate and the object stays absent. REST's environment leg re-raises every fault except "never registered", inside the posture's own `try`, which is the 5xx. ADR bullet 5 names both outcomes. REST's own-kernel leg folds as the dispatcher does; the comment names the environment leg only, which is exact. "The same verdict" replaces "cannot disagree", which was the overstatement.

**Open nits, none blocking:**

- **N1 (follow-up card owed):** the cost of the participant probe on every object list. Unchanged.
- **N2 (accepted deviation):** the once-per-process unusable-delegate notice. Unchanged.
- **N3 (prose):** ADR bullet 2 names no layer. Unchanged; the ADR is not in the delta.

No must-fix and no should-fix is open, so this delta ends the round for the findings of 6844571138.
